title: Final POC readiness ops handshake and cutover checklist

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-12-29
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 47 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE); Priya Nandan (Redwood SE); Tomás Alvarez (Redwood Solutions); Maya Shah (Velora Head of ML); Evan Brooks (Velora Platform Eng); Lina Park (Velora Security); Jon Reed (Velora SRE)

Auto-summary: go/no-go checklist review, telemetry gating, canary thresholds, runbook owners defined.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, quick agenda — recap last weeks metrics, finalize the canary thresholds, confirm A over B split plan and handoff ownership for cutover.
[00:23] Maya Shah: Hi, thanks. we ran the sample week of traffic, saw token cost trends and p95 improved when we enabled the prefix cache but we saw two spikes in latency that matched long prompt flows, so we want to make sure the canary doesn't get overloaded, right.
[00:46] Priya Nandan: Yep, that matches what we saw on the Redwood runtime dashboard — the KV cache warmup took about 8 minutes on cold start, and continuous batching was primed after about 150 requests, so canary should include pre-warm traffic.
[01:15] Evan Brooks: Quick question: on the pre-warm, are we hitting the dedicated instances or the shared hosted lane? because our security team prefers dedicated for PHI handling.
[01:34] Tomás Alvarez: For the pilot we'll route canary to the dedicated pool (the Velora reserved capacity) — fallback is the shared hosted model if capacity dips below threshold, we included that in the fallback policy.
[01:57] Lina Park: I flagged the fallback policy earlier — need to confirm that logs still flow to our audit collector and that keys never leave our VPC. We have KMS rules and HSM requirements.
[02:20] Jordan Lee: Understood. Tomás, can you confirm the KMS handshake works with Redwood's private deployment? Any known exceptions?
[02:34] Tomás Alvarez: Yes, we've tested the KMS envelope flow in staging; the only caveat was an IP range mis-match on Velora side that caused TLS renegotiation, fixed that Tuesday. The rotation cadence is fine, but Lina we do need your final confirmation on the exception list for SOC2.
[02:58] Lina Park: I'll send the exceptions doc tonight.
[03:10] Jordan Lee: Cool. Moving on, canary gating: Priya, walk us through the thresholds you propose.
[03:24] Priya Nandan: Sure — propose three primary gates: p95 latency under 420ms, error rate below 0.7% (5xx/timeout), and quality regression measured by hallucination proxy < 1.5% over the gold prompt set. Also set token-cost-per-1k threshold so we detect runaway prompts.
[03:51] Maya Shah: That hallucination proxy — remind me, how's that computed?
[04:02] Priya Nandan: It's a classification of responses against the gold set; we use entailment heuristics and a small eval model. It's not perfect — expect some false positives, so the gate is the first guard not the final call.
[04:20] Jon Reed: For SLO alerting, we'd like a 5-minute and 30-minute aggregate to differ, so short blips won't block automatically, but sustained degradation will.
[04:36] Evan Brooks: Are we comfortable with the circuit breaker to cut traffic at 2x baseline error rate? What happens to sensitive traffic when that happens?
[04:49] Jordan Lee: The plan is to route to last-stable model snapshot and then to dedicated fallback with reduced throughput. Sensitive PHI flows will be routed to the private VPC lane with stricter throttling.
[05:09] Priya Nandan: Actionable orchestration details: canary will start at 1% for 30 minutes, if gates pass move to 10% for another 30 minutes, then 50% for two hours, then full. Each stage has automated rollback triggers.
[05:33] Maya Shah: That sounds good. For the 10% stage, can we ensure no user-facing errors exceed 0.3%?
[05:45] Priya Nandan: We'll set the per-stage thresholds more strict than baseline, yes.
[06:02] Jordan Lee: Let's talk about the runbook and handoff — Tomás?
[06:10] Tomás Alvarez: I've drafted a runbook with steps: pre-cutover checklist, traffic seed script, monitoring dashboard links, rollback steps, contact list. I'll upload it to our shared drive and tag oncall. It's missing the final alarm thresholds which we need from Velora.
[06:32] Maya Shah: We'll validate thresholds and reply. Also want to add an item to smoke test privacy filter for PHI in the canary responses.
[06:45] Lina Park: On that note, we need to ensure logs redact tokens and PII before leaving the VPC. Is that handled server-side?
[06:57] Tomás Alvarez: Redwood can redact at ingestion level; we have patterns we applied in staging, but we'll need Velora's regex and exception list.
[07:11] Jordan Lee: OK, Maya to send gold prompts and regex, Priya to share canary script.
[07:23] Priya Nandan: I'll push a sample traffic generator and the orchestration playbook; it's a small python script plus k8s job manifest. Note transcription: sometimes file names were munged — script name is canary-runner.py.
[07:42] Evan Brooks: About monitoring, can you call out what metrics the dashboard will include?
[07:50] Priya Nandan: We'll include p50/p95/p99 latencies, token-cost per 1k requests, error-rate (4xx/5xx/timeout), queue depth, KV cache hit rate, model id and kv-cache warmup time, and hallucination proxy. Also retention of logs for 90 days as per the pilot.
[08:21] Maya Shah: 90 days is fine for pilot but production we need 365 days — we can revisit.
[08:31] Jordan Lee: Let's capture the preflight dry-run plan — who owns the staging dry-run?
[08:38] Jon Reed: Velora SRE owns the staging dry-run. We'll run a simulated traffic run with the sample generator and validate the dashboards.
[08:49] Tomás Alvarez: Redwood will provision a prod-sim namespace and seed traffic; we'll coordinate the timing and the exact seed rate.
[09:02] Evan Brooks: Firewall/VPC peering — we need the exact IP list from Redwood and the port list.
[09:11] Tomás Alvarez: We'll send a CIDR list and ports (443, 22 for jumpbox) by EOD.
[09:19] Jordan Lee: Great. Risks — Maya, any concerns remaining?
[09:25] Maya Shah: Biggest worry is model regressions during canary; the hallucination proxy occasionally flags benign rewrites. We need a manual review step if the proxy is tripped during 10% stage.
[09:37] Priya Nandan: Agree — we'll make the 10% stage require manual approval if hallucination proxy crosses 0.8% absolute increase.
[09:48] Lina Park: On compliance — confirm SSO/SAML mapping for RBAC before cutover.
[09:55] Tomás Alvarez: Working with your IdP to map roles, should be done by end of week.
[10:04] Jordan Lee: Ok wrap up, quick recap of owners and deadlines.
[10:10] Priya Nandan: Action items I'll share: canary-runner, sample traffic, orchestration script — due 2027-01-03.
[10:22] Maya Shah: I'll finalize gold set and regex — due 2027-01-02.
[10:30] Evan Brooks: I'll confirm maintenance window — due 2026-12-31.
[10:38] Tomás Alvarez: Runbook upload and oncall tagging — due 2026-12-30.
[10:45] Lina Park: KMS exceptions and SOC2 note — due 2027-01-04.
[10:52] Jordan Lee: Next meeting / go/no-go — scheduled two hours prior to cutover on 2027-01-06, we'll do a staging dry-run on 2027-01-04 02:00 UTC. If anything changes we'll email the thread.
[11:07] Maya Shah: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
